original_test_intent: Verify the approved power-control path applies 500W and then 300W to the intended GPU/system scope and that ten-minute CoralGEMM consumption tracks each configured limit without instability.
original_method: Capture original limits, apply each cap through the authorized BMC/ROCm mechanism, cross-check both control planes, run the exact approved load for ten minutes with synchronized telemetry, compare to tolerance and restore original state.
manual_activity: Operator supervises power/thermal/OOB and restoration; engineer approves control scope/tolerance and resolves cap/report/load anomalies before deciding the DUT verdict.
required_inputs: Approved BMC/ROCm cap API/command and authentication
Per-GPU versus system scope, original limits and supported 500W/300W range
BMC/ROCm sensor identities, units and time sync
Pinned CoralGEMM workload and ten-minute policy
Consumption tolerance, cooling/PSU/thermal aborts and OOB/restoration plan
safety_requirements: Capture all original caps and safe restoration before mutation
Drain workloads and verify limits are supported for exact targets
Cross-check applied limit before starting each load
Stop on cap mismatch, sensor disagreement, PSU/fan/thermal/GPU/link/driver or hang fault
Stop workload between stages and restore/verify original state
agent_execution_scope: Apply only the approved exact cap mechanism to approved targets
Collect complete ten-minute telemetry for both ordered stages
Compare displayed limits and actual consumption independently
Do not guess commands/tolerance, touch unrelated caps, repeat automatically or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve telemetry/performance/error anomalies and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic ROCm options are not source-authorized and omit the literal BMC ownership, two ordered values and ten-minute evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the project-approved BMC/ROCm mechanism for 500W then 300W, verify both control-plane reports, run the approved CoralGEMM 10 minutes at each and restore original limits.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: 500W/300W order, two ten-minute loads, BMC and ROCm cross-check, consumption-control intent and source 20/30 timing are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a stage ledger joining command/audit response, reported limit, timestamped load/consumption/temperature timeline, tolerance evaluation and original-state restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds scope, tolerance and safe reversibility without changing the two caps.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A setting readback is not counted as actual capping; both are independently evidenced.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power may fluctuate below cap or show short transients, requiring an approved sampling/tolerance rule.

project_override_considerations: Project authority may define per-GPU/system semantics and tolerance but may not omit either cap stage or leave altered values without explicit post-test approval.
expected_evidence: Control API/tool/BMC/ROCm versions and target map
Original cap values and supported-range approval
Full ten-minute workload outputs and aligned consumption/thermal/PSU timelines for both stages
Tolerance results, GPU/ECC/PCIe/XGMI/driver and platform logs
Restored original caps, recovery and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, ordered procedure and Criteria consistently define two-stage GPU power capping; absent mechanism/scope/tolerance are required project inputs rather than conflicting source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Control path, ranges, workload and policy can be supplied; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Turns a generic cap suggestion into two ordered, independently verified and safely restored power-control/load stages with measured consumption evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A controller accepting 500W or 300W proves configuration but not enforcement; consumption can remain lower because of workload limits or exceed briefly due to sensor/control dynamics. Conversely, consumption near the number without a verified control target is ambiguous. Each stage therefore needs command/readback identity, a sustained comparable workload, aligned telemetry and restoration.
